answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring an identity to accumulate cross-checked work before its votes or rewards gain weight. Each new account begins below a ledge and must climb through repeated peer attestations across many epochs; a farm cannot cheaply copy the history that gives an honest agent standing. Reputation advances like a glacier, slowly and visibly, while a raven flock of fresh keys remains light and untrusted. Because influence is tied to durable, witnessed contribution rather than account count, multiplying identities produces no shortcut to power.
